name: Kelvex Transit Ground Crew All-Weather Rig
description: A complete daily rig for Kelvex MagRail ground crew — the workers who keep the platforms running between the operator cabin and the maintenance tunnels. The outer layer is a hip-length anorak in Kelvex corporate navy, bonded synth-nylon with reflective silver tape running diagonally across the chest and down both sleeves, bright enough to catch mag-platform floodlights at distance. The Kelvex logo — a stylized K bisected by a transit line — is heat-pressed over the left breast in white, with an embroidered crew number patch on the right. Underneath sits a charcoal ribbed thermal base layer with a half-zip mock neck, tough enough to function as standalone outerwear on mild days. The trousers are Goretek HaulMaster-cut in the same navy, with reinforced knee panels in gunmetal grey ballistic nylon, deep cargo pockets sealed with magnetic closures, and a dedicated tool loop strip along the right thigh. A wide nylon webbing belt in safety orange carries a folding multi-tool, key fob lanyard, and a clip-point for a tablet sleeve. Boots are steel-capped platform treads with anti-static soles and a side-zip for quick removal at shift end. A close-fitting knit cap in charcoal with a single reflective stripe completes the look, often pulled low over a neural port housing on the skull's rear.
functionality: All-weather wind and light-rain resistance, thermal base layer for cold platform tunnels, anti-static soles for electrified rail environments, magnetic cargo pocket closures prevent tool loss on moving platforms, neural port clearance in knit cap, aug-compatible sleeve channels for chrome forearm users
what_it_says: This is someone who shows up, does the work, and goes home. The Kelvex branding signals corporate employment — stable wages, union card, maybe a pension if the corponation honors it. The reflective tape says they work near things that move fast. The worn boot toes and faded knee panels say they've been doing it for years.
worn_by: Kelvex shift supervisors on the floor
manufacturer: Kelvex Transit Systems (corponation-issued uniform, boots sourced from Veldtmann contract)
price_range: Φ180–Φ260 (company-subsidized at Φ40–Φ80 out of pocket for workers)
story_hooks: A ground crew worker finds a deactivated synthetic wedged in the maintenance crawlspace beneath Platform 9 — wearing the same Kelvex uniform, crew number and all, but the synthetic was never on the roster.
The reflective tape on this rig is the exact pattern a witness described seeing flee a mag-platform incident that killed two passengers; the wearer claims they were on the opposite end of the line.
Kelvex has just announced a new automated ground crew rollout — the worker in this rig has two weeks before their position is dissolved, and they've started quietly removing the company patch.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, highly visible transit worker ensemble projecting competence and safety compliance. The silhouette is blocky and functional—broad shoulders from the anorak, tapered through the torso, with cargo-heavy hips and legs grounded by aggressive platform boots. The overall impression is industrial, approachable, and deliberately conspicuous on crowded MagRail platforms.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso for movement and layering; tapered at the waist via the safety-orange webbing belt; cargo pockets sit mid-thigh with intentional volume; boots are snug around the ankle with reinforced heel counter.
physical_description.primary_material: Bonded synth-nylon anorak shell; charcoal ribbed thermal synthetic knit base layer; Goretek ballistic nylon trousers with reinforced knee panels; steel-capped polymer/composite platform boots with anti-static sole matrix
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly waxy nylon exterior with subtle sheen from factory treatment; ribbed thermal knit with tactile depth; matte ballistic nylon on knee reinforcements; aggressive tread pattern on boot sole; nylon webbing with slight friction grip
physical_description.color_scheme: Kelvex corporate navy (anorak, trousers, cap) as dominant; charcoal grey (thermal base, cap); reflective silver tape accents; safety-orange webbing belt; gunmetal grey ballistic panels; white heat-pressed logo and embroidered crew number; black anti-static sole
physical_description.closures: Anorak: full-length main zipper with storm flap; thermal mock-neck: half-zip; trousers: standard fly with magnetic cargo closures; boots: side-zip with reinforced pull tab; belt: friction-lock nylon webbing
distinctive_features: Diagonal and vertical reflective silver tape strips for platform floodlight visibility
Heat-pressed Kelvex K-transit logo on left breast
Embroidered crew number patch on right chest
Reinforced knee panels in contrasting gunmetal ballistic nylon
Dedicated tool loop strip along right thigh with secure clip point
Safety-orange nylon webbing belt with integrated multi-tool carrier and lanyard anchor
Steel-capped platform treads with anti-static conductive soles
Knit cap with single reflective stripe aligned with rear neural port
Magnetic closures on cargo pockets (silent, non-conductive)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 working class—corporation-issued, durable, standardized, but quality construction and reflective safety features signal stable employment in essential infrastructure
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is essential MagRail ground crew: platform maintenance, safety checks, tunnel access, coordination between automated systems and human operators. The uniform signals trustworthiness, visibility, and technical competence. Wearing this in public outside the platform marks someone as transit-sector employed—stable, working-class, infrastructure-aligned.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but maintained—minor creasing from daily movement, small wear marks on knee panels from kneeling, slight fading on the chest logo from sweat and repeated arc-flash exposure, boots scuffed and well-broken-in. Never shabby; corporation maintains minimum standards. Often dusty from mag-rail platform particulate.
